stem:
Rohan needs a sense of how many seats are in the school hall so he can order refreshments. There are about 20 rows with about 15 seats in each row. An exact seat count is not needed.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: An estimate near 300 seats is enough for this purpose.
Estimation means treating $20 \times 15$ as an exact census of every seat.
Exact counting is what produces estimates, so he must finish a full seat tally first.
Refreshment planning requires the perimeter of the hall, not a seat count.

teacher.key_rationale: About 20×15 gives a usable estimate near 300 when an exact count is unnecessary. An estimate is not a finished census. Exact counting is not a prerequisite for estimating. Perimeter is a different quantity.
